scope: UTIAS In-The-Dark night runs 000017/000018: range-extract metadata + selected stereo frames, compose/verify GT, run hand-written SIFT+SGBM front-end + robust layer, day-vs-night comparison
status: measured (both night runs, 10 pairs each, 1,674 zip64 offsets and 2 extraction bugs fixed)

fetched_bytes.note: run_000017 images 10,932,166 B + metadata 511,227 B; run_000018 images ~9.10 MB + metadata 485,749 B; plus ~6.5 MB repeated central-directory reads; vs whole zips 5,367,290,174 B

rounds.hypothesis: The 2.76 GB night archive can be listed from a 128 KB tail probe + central directory without downloading the whole zip (direct FTP is ~14 KB/s).
rounds.change: Ran the range extractor in list mode through the working SOCKS5 proxy; parsed all central-directory entries and their compressed/uncompressed sizes.
rounds.metric_before_after: Before: 0 B of night metadata, whole-zip ETA ~55 h. After: 7,546 members listed (7,542 images + transforms_spatial.txt 1,061,397 B + timestamps_images.txt 96,936 B + gps.txt 128,242 B + timestamps_gps.txt 89,786 B); tail 131,072 B + central directory 537,032 B in 15.8 s.

rounds.hypothesis: transforms_spatial.txt (1.06 MB uncompressed) and timestamps_images.txt can be range-extracted with CRC verification.
rounds.change: Extracted the four non-image members with fetch_zip_members.py (raw deflate + size + CRC32 check per member).
rounds.command: ALL_PROXY=socks5h://127.0.0.1:7899 $PY fetch_zip_members.py --url 'ftp://asrl3.utias.utoronto.ca/2020-vtr-dataset/UTIAS-In-The-Dark/run_000017.zip' --size 2761424974 --member transforms_spatial.txt --member timestamps_images.txt --member gps.txt --member timestamps_gps.txt --out-dir /mnt/storage1/syk/data/utias_in_the_dark/run_000017
rounds.metric_before_after: Before: no night GT/timestamps. After: 1,376,361 B uncompressed from 511,227 B deflate, all CRC ok, 37.2 s; 3,771 vertices, timestamps span 2016-07-19 21:58:56-22:09:49 UTC (652.9 s).

rounds.hypothesis: The same range protocol works on the second night run (2,605,865,200 B).
rounds.change: Extracted transforms_spatial.txt, timestamps_images.txt, gps.txt, timestamps_gps.txt for run_000018.
rounds.command: ALL_PROXY=socks5h://127.0.0.1:7899 $PY fetch_zip_members.py --url 'ftp://asrl3.utias.utoronto.ca/2020-vtr-dataset/UTIAS-In-The-Dark/run_000018.zip' --size 2605865200 --member transforms_spatial.txt --member timestamps_images.txt --member gps.txt --member timestamps_gps.txt --out-dir /mnt/storage1/syk/data/utias_in_the_dark/run_000018
rounds.metric_before_after: Before: no run_000018 metadata. After: 999,850 B spatial + 91,216 B timestamps + 130,277 B gps + 91,216 B ts_gps (485,749 B deflate), CRC ok; 3,551 vertices, 682.1 s span.

rounds.hypothesis: Night image members can be extracted exactly like the metadata members.
rounds.change: Inspected the central directory: 1,674 of 7,546 image entries (22%) store local-header offset 0xFFFFFFFF and put the real 8-byte offset in the zip64 extra field (header id 0x0001, 12 B); patched fetch_zip_members.py to resolve it before extracting.
rounds.metric_before_after: Before patch: those 1,674 members would be fetched from offset 0xFFFFFFFF (garbage, CRC failure). After: two test members extracted with size+CRC ok (349,836 B and 392,218 B), both decode as 512x384 RGB PNG.
rounds.decision: keep the zip64 fix (code change in fetch_zip_members.py)

rounds.hypothesis: One extractor call can fetch left and right frames of a window into the run directory.
rounds.change: Flat output wrote both images/left/002712.png and images/right/002712.png to the same basename and silently overwrote one; changed fetch_zip_members.py to preserve images/left|right/ member paths.
rounds.metric_before_after: Before: 13 of 26 files silently lost to basename collisions. After: 11 left + 11 right files in separate images/left|right dirs, all 22 decode and are 384x512; left-image mean intensity 96.5-99.2.

rounds.hypothesis: The repeat-spatial x teach-temporal composition validated on daylight runs also resolves night consecutive pairs.
rounds.change: Ran compose_pairs/gt_pairs on run_000017 against the existing teach_meta (transforms_temporal.txt already range-extracted from run_000000).
rounds.metric_before_after: Before: 0 composed night pairs. After: 3,769 of 3,770 consecutive pairs resolvable (1 skipped only because a spatial match jumps -1,106 teach vertices > max_teach_jump=4); teach gaps {0: 2674, +1: 1085, +2: 10}.

rounds.hypothesis: Same composition works for the second night run.
rounds.change: Composed run_000018 GT with the same convention 'ba' and camera-frame conjugation.
rounds.metric_before_after: Before: 0. After: 3,549 of 3,550 pairs resolvable (1 skipped: -1,105 teach jump); gaps {0: 2451, +1: 1089, +2: 8, -1: 1}.

rounds.hypothesis: Night windows must be picked from GT motion only (not front-end results) and should match the daylight motion scale for a fair comparison.
rounds.change: Scanned all 10-pair windows in the composed GT, chose the maximum-median-|t| window per run; then probed brightness on the selected left frames before committing to the image fetch.
rounds.command: $PY - <<'PY' ... compose_pairs + sliding window median t_norm/rot ... PY
rounds.metric_before_after: Before: unknown window, daylight baseline |t|=0.123 m. After: run_000017 start 2712 (|t| median 0.215 m, rot 0.62 deg, all 10 pairs jump<=2); run_000018 start 2529 (0.206 m, 0.69 deg); probed left means 95.8 / 89.4 / 96.5 / 99.8 (frames 200/500/2712/3000 of run_000017), so frames are dark but not featureless.
rounds.decision: keep - pre-registered window choice, matched |t| to daylight control

rounds.hypothesis: Fetching 22 images serially with one curl per member is fast enough (<5 min).
rounds.change: Measured serial fetch_zip_members.py on a 2-image call (central directory + two members).
rounds.metric_before_after: Before: assumed 22 images ~2 min. After: 46.9 s for 742 KB of members (effective ~16 KB/s incl. 668 KB central-directory re-read); 22 images projected >15 min per run, rejected.
rounds.decision: revert the serial path for images

rounds.hypothesis: The FTP limit is per connection; parallel range requests raise aggregate throughput.
rounds.change: Wrote fetch_night_images.py: parse the cached central directory once, then thread pool of range requests, each decompressed with size+CRC32 check.
rounds.metric_before_after: Before: ~7 KB/s serial. After: 10 of 16 members in 26.7 s (aggregate ~150-200 KB/s), but 6 requests died with curl (28) timeouts.
rounds.decision: keep the parallel fetcher; tune worker count

rounds.hypothesis: 12 concurrent FTP connections exceed the server/proxy limit; 6 should be stable.
rounds.change: Retried the remaining members at 6 workers, then fetched the full run_000017 window at 6 workers.
rounds.metric_before_after: Before (12 workers): 6/16 curl-28 timeouts on run_000018. After (6 workers): run_000018 5/6 in 14.6 s + last 1 in 2 workers; run_000017 all 22 images in 34.5 s, no timeouts, all PNGs decode.

rounds.hypothesis: A concurrent sibling process fetching the same night run into the same directory does not corrupt our extraction.
rounds.change: Detected pid 3153114 (worktree wt-final-p3) fetching run_000017 frames 000000-000015 into /mnt/storage1/syk/data/utias_in_the_dark/run_000017 and sharing .tmp/member.bin; stopped sharing that path and staged our window in night17_stage/night18_stage with separate .tmp, copying verified images in afterwards.
rounds.metric_before_after: Before: both writers use run_000017/.tmp/member.bin -> read-after-write race could corrupt ranges. After: isolated staging, 22+22 images CRC-verified and decode-checked; no shared-file failure observed.

rounds.hypothesis: verify_inthedark.py (row alignment, GT vs inverse/identity/conjugated, decode/size) passes on night pairs.
rounds.change: First run failed because the window was addressed by sorted-pair index while one earlier pair is skipped, so --start 2712 selects 2713->...->2723 and frame 002723 was missing; fetched that boundary frame and re-ran.
rounds.metric_before_after: Before: FileNotFoundError at vertex 2723 (index/vertex-id off-by-one). After: 6/6 checks PASS - GT reproj 0.57 px (0.47-0.75), inverse 24.27 px, identity 12.74 px, vehicle-frame (no conjugation) 20.40 px, median row dy 0.49 px, depth 3.49 m.

rounds.hypothesis: The same six checks pass on the second night run.
rounds.change: Same index/vertex-id boundary issue (frame 002540 missing) fixed by fetching it; re-ran verification.
rounds.metric_before_after: Before: FileNotFoundError at vertex 2540. After: 6/6 checks PASS - GT 0.51 px (0.38-0.79), inverse 23.53 px, identity 12.28 px, vehicle 19.82 px, row dy 0.50 px, depth 3.38 m.

rounds.hypothesis: The hand-written SIFT+SGBM front-end may fail on dark night frames; quantify honestly if it does.
rounds.change: Ran run_inthedark.py with dense SGBM on 10 night pairs at the pre-selected max-motion window (start 2712).
rounds.metric_before_after: Before: unknown (day dense baseline 79.4% inliers, GNC 0.078 deg / 0.020 m). After: natural inlier rate 96.0% [95.1,97.8], 481 correspondences, depth 4.6 m, GT |t| 0.218 m / rot 0.59 deg; GNC-GM 0.135 deg / 0.011 m, success@0.1 m 100%, wall 2.8 s, front-end 160 ms/pair.
rounds.decision: keep - night frames are usable by this front-end

rounds.hypothesis: The night result replicates on the second run/window.
rounds.change: Dense SGBM on 10 pairs at start 2529.
rounds.metric_before_after: Before: unknown. After: inlier 97.1% [95.4,98.3], 480 corr, depth 4.5 m, GT |t| 0.214 m / rot 0.69 deg; GNC 0.150 deg / 0.011 m, success@0.1 m 100%, wall 2.7 s.

rounds.hypothesis: Sparse triangulation is more outlier-sensitive than dense SGBM at night, as it was in daylight.
rounds.metric_before_after: Before: day sparse 66.7% inliers / GNC 0.103 deg / 0.011 m. After: night sparse 84.3% [70.9,87.2], 201 corr, depth 3.9 m; GNC 0.197 deg / 0.015 m, success@0.1 m 100%, wall 3.2 s; naive Kabsch only 20% -> robust layer still recovers 100%.
rounds.decision: keep as the second night config; dense remains the headline

rounds.hypothesis: Higher night inlier rate could be a lighting effect; a motion-matched daylight window would separate lighting from geometry.
rounds.change: Found a daylight window in run_000002 with |t|=0.21 m / rot 0.54 deg (comparable to night 0.21-0.22 m / 0.59-0.69 deg) and ran the same dense pipeline.
rounds.metric_before_after: Before: day start-200 baseline 79.4% inliers / 7.2 m depth / GNC 0.078 deg / 0.020 m. After matched control: 85.9% [84.8,88.3], 850 corr, depth 6.7 m, |t| 0.208 m; GNC 0.121 deg / 0.007 m, success 100%. Night inliers are higher but night depth is 4.5 m vs 6.7 m, so the gain is geometric, not a lighting robustness claim.
rounds.decision: keep - rules out the 'SIFT is more robust at night' reading

rounds.hypothesis: Night numbers can be reported without hand-typing and with the daylight comparison in one place.
rounds.change: Wrote summarize_night.py (renders results/night_main.md + results/night_summary.json from the JSONs), updated the inthedark README (conclusion, fetch pitfalls, night table, verify table, reproduction, limitations) and this round log.
rounds.metric_before_after: Before: night section absent; README said night runs unmeasured. After: 6 configs summarized, 19 documented rounds, ~21 MB useful member bytes fetched (≈27 MB incl. repeated central-directory reads) versus 5,367,290,174 B of night zips (~200-250x); no commit/push.
